summary:
The Prohibiting Russian Uranium Imports Act amends section 3112A of the USEC Privatization Act (42 U.S.C. § 2297h-10a) to prohibit specified imports of Russian-origin low-enriched uranium into the United States, subject to limited waiver authority, exceptions, and a statutory sunset.

Section 2(a) adds a new subsection 3112A(d). New subsection (d)(1), effective beginning 90 days after enactment, prohibits importation into the United States of (A) unirradiated low-enriched uranium produced in the Russian Federation or by a “Russian entity,” and (B) unirradiated low-enriched uranium determined to have been exchanged with, swapped for, or otherwise obtained in lieu of such uranium in a manner designed to circumvent section 3112A. New subsection (d)(5) defines “Russian entity” as an entity organized under the laws of, or otherwise subject to the jurisdiction of, the Government of the Russian Federation.

New subsection (d)(2) authorizes the Secretary of Energy, in consultation with the Secretaries of State and Commerce, to waive the prohibition if the Secretary of Energy determines either that no alternative viable source of low-enriched uranium is available to sustain the continued operation of a nuclear reactor or United States nuclear energy company, or that the importation is in the national interest. Waived imports remain subject to annual aggregate quantity limitations: 476,536 kilograms in calendar year 2024; 470,376 kilograms in 2025; 464,183 kilograms in 2026; and 459,083 kilograms in 2027, including uranium obtained under contracts for separative work units and whether or not derived from highly enriched uranium of weapons origin. The Secretary of Commerce must administer and enforce those limitations in accordance with the Suspension Agreement, including specified provisions referenced in section 3112A(c)(2)(B)(i), and in a manner imposing minimal burden on the commercial nuclear industry. Any waiver must terminate not later than January 1, 2028, and the Secretary of Energy must notify specified House and Senate committees upon issuance, identifying the waiver recipient.

New subsection (d)(3) excludes from the prohibition imports by or under contract to the Department of Energy for national security or nonproliferation purposes, and imports of non-uranium isotopes. New subsection (d)(4) terminates subsection (d) on December 31, 2040.

Section 2(b) makes conforming amendments to section 3112A(c), including striking clauses (xi) through (xxvii) of paragraph (2)(A), revising cross-references, striking paragraph (5), redesignating paragraphs (6) through (12) as paragraphs (5) through (11), and replacing a December 31, 2040 date in redesignated paragraph (8) with the effective date described in new subsection (d)(1). Section 2(b)(2) provides that the amendment to section 3112A(c)(2)(A)(xi) takes effect 90 days after enactment.
